nodes.label: lpl
nodes.def: long_parameter_list: a method or function whose parameter signature exceeds a comfortable cognitive threshold, typically citing more than three or four distinct arguments, making t

nodes.label: coc 001
nodes.def: commented_code_element: a syntactic unit of source code that has been rendered inactive by enclosing it in comment syntax, producing no observable execution behavior while remainin

nodes.label: bloaters
nodes.def: Code smells indicating structures that have grown excessively large and difficult to work with.

nodes.label: brain overload
nodes.def: Cognitive complexity where a class or method requires too much context to understand, straining working memory.

nodes.label: couplers
nodes.def: Code smells indicating excessive or inappropriate dependencies between classes and modules.

nodes.label: dispensables
nodes.def: Code smells for unnecessary or vestigial elements that could be removed without losing functionality.

nodes.label: primitive obsession
nodes.def: Using primitive types where small objects would provide better semantics, type safety, and expressiveness.

nodes.label: refused bequest
nodes.def: A subclass using only some inherited methods, suggesting inheritance hierarchy is wrong or composition preferred.

nodes.label: data clump
nodes.def: A group of variables appearing together in multiple locations, indicating a missing class or abstraction.

nodes.label: duplicated code
nodes.def: Identical or nearly identical code fragments appearing in multiple locations, violating DRY principle.

nodes.label: large class
nodes.def: A class containing too many responsibilities, fields, or lines of code indicating violation of single responsibility.

nodes.label: long method
nodes.def: A method that has grown too large, typically exceeding dozens of lines, making it hard to understand and maintain.

nodes.label: oop abusers
nodes.def: Code smells indicating incorrect or incomplete use of object-oriented constructs and patterns.

nodes.label: speculative generality
nodes.def: Classes, methods, or parameters added in anticipation of future needs that never materialized.

nodes.label: anemic domain model
nodes.def: A domain model consisting of data classes lacking the business logic that should be encapsulated within the objects themselves.

nodes.label: boy scout rule
nodes.def: Principle urging leaving code slightly cleaner than found, enabling incremental refactoring.

nodes.label: change preventers
nodes.def: Code smells requiring changes in multiple places when a single responsibility changes.

nodes.label: dead code
nodes.def: Code executed but producing no observable effect, or code that can never be executed, increasing maintenance burden.

nodes.label: inappropriate intimacy
nodes.def: Two classes with excessive coupling, accessing each other's private details in inappropriate ways.

nodes.label: message chain
nodes.def: A series of chained method calls like a.getB().getC().getD(), creating tight coupling across the chain.

nodes.label: middle man
nodes.def: A class delegating almost all work to another class, indicating unnecessary indirection or missing abstraction.

nodes.label: refactoring
nodes.def: Disciplined restructuring of code to improve internal quality without altering external behavior or functionality.

nodes.label: refactoring catalog
nodes.def: An organized collection of documented refactoring patterns paired with the specific code smells each addresses.

nodes.label: shotgun surgery
nodes.def: A single change requires modifying many classes, indicating responsibilities are scattered across types.

nodes.label: temporary field
nodes.def: Fields in a class populated only under certain conditions, indicating missing abstraction or state pattern.

nodes.label: agile refactoring
nodes.def: Refactoring practices aligned with agile values: continuous improvement, embracing change, sustainable pace.

nodes.label: behavior changing refactoring
nodes.def: Refactoring that intentionally changes behavior, requiring corresponding test updates and verification.

nodes.label: behavior preserving refactoring
nodes.def: Refactoring that maintains all observable behavior, enabling verification through existing tests.

nodes.label: branch by abstraction
nodes.def: Pattern using abstraction layer to enable safe migration between implementations without big-bang rewrite.

nodes.label: change frequency metric
nodes.def: Measure of how often a field group is modified or extended together.

nodes.label: class
nodes.def: Primitive: a type defining fields and methods as a cohesive unit.

nodes.label: coc 009
nodes.def: confusion_signal: the observable cognitive overhead or maintenance uncertainty experienced by an observer when encountering commented-out code without clear justification.

nodes.label: code inspection
nodes.def: Structured examination of source code artifacts to assess quality and identify improvement opportunities.

nodes.label: code smell
nodes.def: A surface indication that usually corresponds to a deeper problem in system design or implementation, not a bug.

nodes.label: code smell detection
nodes.def: Process of identifying and classifying code smells for prioritization and remediation.

nodes.label: coupling metric
nodes.def: Measure of interdependency between modules, with high coupling indicating design weakness.

nodes.label: data class
nodes.def: A class containing only data fields with accessors and mutators, lacking meaningful behavior.

nodes.label: dc 001
nodes.def: A data_clump is a group of two or more variables that appear together as a repeated pattern across three or more distinct call sites or declarations, indicating a missing cohesive

nodes.label: divergent change
nodes.def: A class requiring modification for multiple unrelated reasons, indicating too many responsibilities.

nodes.label: extract class
nodes.def: Refactoring to split a class with too many responsibilities into two or more cohesive classes.

nodes.label: extract interface
nodes.def: Refactoring to extract a common interface from multiple classes with shared behavior contracts.

nodes.label: extract method
nodes.def: Refactoring to replace a code fragment with a method call, reducing length and improving named abstraction.

nodes.label: feature envy
nodes.def: A method more interested in data of other classes than its own, suggesting the method belongs elsewhere.

nodes.label: linter
nodes.def: Static analysis tool enforcing coding conventions and detecting code smells automatically.

nodes.label: long parameter list
nodes.def: A function or method requiring excessive parameters, suggesting missing abstraction or parameter object.

nodes.label: lpl introduce param obj
nodes.def: introduce_parameter_object_refactoring: a transformation that replaces a long parameter list with a single parameter object class, grouping related data and enabling method reuse a

nodes.label: lpl primitive bundle
nodes.def: primitive_parameter_bundle: a set of primitive values that travel together through multiple method signatures, frequently indicating a missing abstraction that could be encapsulate

nodes.label: missing abstraction
nodes.def: Situations where behavior is embedded in concrete data structures rather than meaningful abstractions.

nodes.label: move method
nodes.def: Refactoring to relocate a method to a class where it belongs, reducing inappropriate intimacy.

nodes.label: opportunistic refactoring
nodes.def: Refactoring done opportunistically when code is touched for other reasons, per Beck's rule of three.

nodes.label: regression test
nodes.def: Test ensuring refactored code continues to produce identical behavior, serving as safety net.

nodes.label: static analysis
nodes.def: Automated tool examining source code to detect patterns corresponding to known smells.

nodes.label: strangler fig pattern
nodes.def: Incremental refactoring strategy replacing legacy system by growing new system around edges.

nodes.label: switch statement smell
nodes.def: Repeated switch statements across code paths, suggesting need for polymorphism or lookup table.

nodes.label: technical debt
nodes.def: The implied cost of future rework caused by choosing expedient solutions over better approaches now.

nodes.label: trivial getter
nodes.def: A getter that merely returns an internal field with zero transformation or business meaning.

nodes.label: abstraction gap
nodes.def: The absence of domain logic, facts, or invariants that should govern the data held by the class.

nodes.label: accessor method
nodes.def: A method that returns a field value directly without transformation or business logic.

nodes.label: accessor mutator pair
nodes.def: A matched getter and setter that expose a single data field with no intervening logic.

nodes.label: accessor primitive
nodes.def: An operation that reads state without modification.

nodes.label: anemic state holder
nodes.def: A data class reduced to holding state without the behavior responsible for maintaining that state's integrity.

nodes.label: antipattern
nodes.def: Common response to recurring problems that is ineffective and creates new problems.

nodes.label: bastard data class
nodes.def: A data class that accumulates responsibility over time, violating single responsibility, often from premature aggregation of unrelated fields.

nodes.label: behavior primitive
nodes.def: Meaningful logic that operates on or validates state.

nodes.label: brittle signature
nodes.def: A method or function signature that requires frequent modification when new fields are added.

nodes.label: class primitive
nodes.def: A blueprint for objects, grouping state and behavior.

nodes.label: clump candidate
nodes.def: A set of fields or parameters identified as recurring together and eligible for extraction.

nodes.label: coc 002
nodes.def: comment_syntax_container: the comment delimiters and surrounding text that physically bind the disabled code element, making its source legible but its semantics inert.

nodes.label: coc 003
nodes.def: dead_execution_state: the condition of a code element whose source text exists but whose semantics are excluded from runtime interpretation.

nodes.label: coc 004
nodes.def: rationale_annotation: an explanatory comment accompanying commented-out code that documents the reason for its disablement, often speculative or stale.

nodes.label: coc 005
nodes.def: temporal_marker: metadata within or adjacent to commented code that indicates when it was disabled, such as a date, version number, or commit reference.

nodes.label: coc 006
nodes.def: resurrection_intent: an expressed or implied intention within commented code to re-enable it in the future, typically indicated by TODO, FIXME, or similar markers.

nodes.label: coc 007
nodes.def: version_control_anchor: the commit, branch, or revision at which the code element was disabled, serving as the authoritative record of its prior active state.

nodes.label: coc 008
nodes.def: observer_agent: a developer or automated system that encounters commented-out code during maintenance, reading, or modification activities.

nodes.label: coc 010
nodes.def: maintenance_burden: the increased cost of change—measured in time, risk, or error likelihood—imposed by commented-out code on future development activities.

nodes.label: coc 011
nodes.def: code_smell: a surface indicator in source code that suggests a potential deeper problem in design or implementation, of which commented-out code is one instance.

nodes.label: coc 012
nodes.def: substitution_pair: an active code element that replaces or is intended to replace a commented-out element, establishing a functional successor relationship.

nodes.label: code quality metric
nodes.def: Quantitative measure of code properties like cyclomatic complexity, coupling, cohesion, or LOC.

nodes.label: code review
nodes.def: Manual examination of code changes to identify smells before they enter codebase permanently.

nodes.label: code rot
nodes.def: Progressive degradation of code quality and maintainability over time through accumulated small changes.

nodes.label: cohesion metric
nodes.def: Measure of how related elements within a module are, with low cohesion indicating missed abstractions.

nodes.label: collapse hierarchy
nodes.def: Refactoring to merge similar superclass and subclass when distinction has eroded.

nodes.label: commented out code
nodes.def: Disabled code left in place, creating confusion and noise; should be deleted and version-controlled instead.

nodes.label: complexity metric
nodes.def: Quantitative measure like cyclomatic complexity indicating difficulty of understanding and testing code.

nodes.label: composite refactoring
nodes.def: Sequence of refactorings applied together to transform a significant portion of code structure.

nodes.label: consolidate duplicate conditional fragments
nodes.def: Refactoring to move repeated code outside branches of conditional, reducing duplication.

nodes.label: coupling symptom
nodes.def: Tight coupling arising when callers depend directly on the class's internal data structure and mutators.

nodes.label: cyclic dependency
nodes.def: Mutual dependencies forming cycles between modules, preventing independent deployment and testing.

nodes.label: data field
nodes.def: A field that stores data without associated computation or validation logic.

nodes.label: decompose conditional
nodes.def: Refactoring to extract condition and each branch into named methods, improving conditional readability.

nodes.label: dry principle
nodes.def: Don't Repeat Yourself principle violated by duplicated code smell, urging single source of truth.

nodes.label: field
nodes.def: Primitive: a named member variable of a class or struct.

nodes.label: field primitive
nodes.def: A named slot holding state within a class.

nodes.label: form template method
nodes.def: Refactoring to extract varying steps of similar algorithms into template method pattern.

nodes.label: god class
nodes.def: An extreme case of large class with hundreds of fields and methods, absorbing too many responsibilities.

nodes.label: god method
nodes.def: An extreme case of long method containing thousands of lines, often containing unrelated logic.

nodes.label: incremental refactoring
nodes.def: Small-step refactoring accumulating into significant structural improvement without large risky changes.

nodes.label: inline class
nodes.def: Refactoring to collapse a class whose responsibilities are trivial into its collaborating classes.

nodes.label: introduce null object
nodes.def: Refactoring to replace null checks with null object instances, encapsulating null handling behavior.

nodes.label: introduce parameter object
nodes.def: Refactoring to replace long parameter lists with a parameter object, grouping related data.

nodes.label: lazy class
nodes.def: A class that does not justify its own existence, having minimal responsibilities and low cohesion.

nodes.label: liskov substitution principle
nodes.def: Principle that subtypes must be substitutable for base types, violated by refused bequest.

nodes.label: lpl caller clone
nodes.def: caller_signature_clone: a pattern where multiple call sites pass the same subset of parameters to a method, signaling that those parameters form a logical unit awaiting formalizati

nodes.label: lpl change ripple
nodes.def: signature_change_ripple: the cascade of modifications required across all call sites when a long parameter list is altered, representing the brittleness cost of the current design

nodes.label: lpl cognitive load
nodes.def: parameter_cognitive_load: the mental effort required to recall the order, type, and purpose of each argument at every call site, which degrades rapidly as parameter count increases

nodes.label: lpl data clump rel
nodes.def: data_clump_association: the kinship between long_parameter_list and data_clump, where the same fields appear together repeatedly across methods and constructors, both pointing towa

nodes.label: lpl extract helper
nodes.def: extract_parameter_grouping_method: splitting a long-parameter method into smaller methods that each receive a coherent subset of parameters, addressing the long method smell alongs

nodes.label: lpl invariant leak
nodes.def: cross_parameter_invariant: a constraint or business rule that logically spans two or more separate parameters but cannot be enforced because the parameters lack a shared container

nodes.label: lpl long method rel
nodes.def: long_method_cooccurrence: the empirical pattern that methods with long parameter lists frequently also suffer from excessive length and complexity, as both stem from insufficient d

nodes.label: lpl preserve whole
nodes.def: preserve_whole_object_refactoring: a technique that passes the source object itself rather than extracting and passing individual attributes, reducing parameter count by restoring

nodes.label: lpl primitive obsession rel
nodes.def: primitive_obsession_association: the tendency to pass multiple primitives instead of a richer object, feeding the long_parameter_list problem and suggesting that introducing a para

nodes.label: lpl replace param method
nodes.def: replace_parameter_with_method_call: a refactoring that eliminates a parameter by having the method obtain the value itself, applicable when the callee can compute the argument from

nodes.label: lpl test constructor
nodes.def: test_fixture_burden: the difficulty of constructing meaningful test cases when a method requires many parameters, often leading to tests that omit or default critical arguments

nodes.label: lpl threshold
nodes.def: parameter_count_threshold: the line of demarcation beyond which a parameter list is deemed excessive, commonly cited as three to four parameters in literature, though context and t

nodes.label: martin fowler catalog
nodes.def: The canonical refactoring catalog from Fowler's book, mapping smells to specific refactoring moves.

nodes.label: michael feathers smells
nodes.def: Smells identified by Feathers including ones that inhibit testing and safe refactoring.

nodes.label: open closed principle
nodes.def: Principle that classes should be open for extension but closed for modification, violated by shotgun surgery.

nodes.label: parallel inheritance
nodes.def: Parallel class hierarchies requiring corresponding subclasses in each, indicating coupled abstractions.

nodes.label: planned refactoring
nodes.def: Deliberate refactoring effort scheduled and resourced separately from feature development work.

nodes.label: preserving behavior
nodes.def: Core invariant of refactoring: transformations must not change observable program behavior.

nodes.label: pull up method
nodes.def: Refactoring to move a method from subclass to shared superclass, reducing duplication across hierarchy.

nodes.label: push down method
nodes.def: Refactoring to move a method from superclass to specific subclass, increasing specificity.

nodes.label: refactoring antipattern
nodes.def: Anti-pattern where refactoring creates new problems or fails to address root causes.

nodes.label: remove dead code
nodes.def: Refactoring to delete code that no longer contributes to program behavior or output.

nodes.label: rename method
nodes.def: Refactoring to change an identifier to better reveal intent and improve code communication.

nodes.label: replace conditional with polymorphism
nodes.def: Refactoring to replace type-checking conditionals with polymorphic dispatch, eliminating switch smell.

nodes.label: replace delegation with inheritance
nodes.def: Refactoring to replace delegation chain with inheritance when appropriate abstraction emerges.

nodes.label: replace inheritance with delegation
nodes.def: Refactoring to replace inheritance with delegation when a class only uses part of parent.

nodes.label: replace magic number
nodes.def: Refactoring to replace numeric literals with named constants, improving intent communication.

nodes.label: replace nested conditionals with guard clauses
nodes.def: Refactoring to use early returns for edge cases instead of deep nesting, improving clarity.

nodes.label: replace primitive with object
nodes.def: Refactoring to replace primitive values with small objects providing richer type and behavior.

nodes.label: replace temp with query
nodes.def: Refactoring to replace temporary variables with method calls, making state implicit and localized.

nodes.label: replace type code with class
nodes.def: Refactoring to replace numeric type codes with meaningful classes, improving type safety.

nodes.label: replace type code with state
nodes.def: Refactoring to replace type codes with state objects when behavior varies with the type.

nodes.label: replace type code with subclasses
nodes.def: Refactoring to replace type codes with inheritance hierarchy when behavior varies per type.

nodes.label: self encapsulate field
nodes.def: Refactoring to add getter and setter methods for direct field access, enabling subclass customization.

nodes.label: single responsibility principle
nodes.def: Principle that a class should have only one reason to change, violated by divergent change smell.

nodes.label: solid principles
nodes.def: Design principles (single responsibility, open-closed, Liskov substitution, interface segregation, dependency inversion) guiding refactoring targets.

nodes.label: test after refactoring
nodes.def: Practice of verifying refactored code produces same outputs as original, ensuring behavior preservation.

nodes.label: yagni principle
nodes.def: You Aren't Gonna Need It principle violated by speculative generality smell.

nodes.label: dc 002
nodes.def: A clump instance is a concrete occurrence where a specific set of variable names or types travel together as a bound unit across multiple locations.

nodes.label: dc 003
nodes.def: A clump signature is the canonical ordered set of variable names and types that define a recurring data group, used to match equivalent clumps across sites.

nodes.label: dc 004
nodes.def: A clump site is a distinct lexical location where the clump variables appear together, such as a function signature, method call, or field declaration.

nodes.label: dc 005
nodes.def: Parameter clump is a data_clump that manifests as a group of method or function parameters that repeat together across multiple call sites.

nodes.label: dc 006
nodes.def: State clump is a data_clump that manifests as a group of instance or class fields that are always initialized or mutated together.

nodes.label: dc 007
nodes.def: Contextual clump is a data_clump where the same primitive variables appear together but only within a specific subsystem or feature boundary.

nodes.label: dc 008
nodes.def: Missing abstraction is the root cause condition where no class, struct, or record type encapsulates a recurring variable group, forcing clients to manage the group manually.

nodes.label: dc 009
nodes.def: Clump threshold is the minimum repetition count (typically three or more distinct sites) required before a variable group qualifies as a detected data_clump smell.

nodes.label: dc 010
nodes.def: Clump extraction is the refactoring operation that introduces a new type to represent the data group and replaces repeated variable declarations with instances of the new type.

nodes.label: dc abstraction surrogate
nodes.def: the new parameter or field of candidate_abstraction type that replaces the entire clump_instance at a call site.

nodes.label: dc candidate abstraction
nodes.def: a candidate class or record type whose fields would mirror the clump_instance members, enabling replacement of the raw variables with a typed object.

nodes.label: dc clump instance
nodes.def: a concrete occurrence of a data_clump: a specific set of variables that repeatedly co-appear in code.

nodes.label: dc cooccurrence count
nodes.def: an integer metric: the number of distinct call sites or scopes where the same variable set appears together.

nodes.label: dc cooccurrence threshold
nodes.def: an integer metric: the minimum cooccurrence_count that qualifies a variable set as a clump_instance (commonly two or more).

nodes.label: dc root
nodes.def: data_clump — a recurring group of two or more variables passed together through multiple signatures or used together across multiple scopes, indicating a missing abstraction.

nodes.label: dc situation field
nodes.def: a clump_instance whose co-occurred variables are instance fields of one or more classes.

nodes.label: dc situation local
nodes.def: a clump_instance whose co-occurred variables appear as locals within one or more method bodies.

nodes.label: dc situation parameter
nodes.def: a clump_instance whose co-occurred variables are formal parameters of one or more method signatures.

nodes.label: dc smell anchor
nodes.def: a code location where the clump_instance appears, serving as a refactoring entry point.

nodes.label: dc variable member
nodes.def: one constituent field or parameter within a clump_instance, considered in isolation before grouping.

nodes.label: debt metaphor
nodes.def: Metaphor framing quality shortcuts as debt accruing interest through maintenance costs until repaid.

nodes.label: dependency inversion principle
nodes.def: Principle that high-level modules should not depend on low-level modules, violated by inappropriate intimacy.

nodes.label: divergent modularity
nodes.def: Classes that evolve independently without shared abstractions, creating unnecessary duplication.

nodes.label: dto
nodes.def: Data Transfer Object: a legitimate data class variant whose sole purpose is to carry data across system boundaries.

nodes.label: encapsulation illusion
nodes.def: Accessors and mutators expose internal state, defeating information hiding despite appearing encapsulated.

nodes.label: exposed internal state
nodes.def: Data class internals exposed directly to callers without encapsulation or abstraction boundary.

nodes.label: extract variable
nodes.def: Refactoring to assign a meaningful name to an intermediate expression, improving readability.

nodes.label: inline method
nodes.def: Refactoring to replace a method body with its call when the method body is as clear as the name.

nodes.label: interface segregation principle
nodes.def: Principle that clients should not depend on interfaces they do not use, violated by interface pollution.

nodes.label: method
nodes.def: Primitive: a named unit of behavior accepting parameters and operating on fields.

nodes.label: missing behavior
nodes.def: Behavior that logically belongs in a data class but has not been implemented, leaving it anemic.

nodes.label: mutator method
nodes.def: A method that assigns a field value directly without validation or side effects.

nodes.label: mutator primitive
nodes.def: An operation that modifies state.

nodes.label: naming pattern
nodes.def: Conventional suffixes or prefixes identifying data-holding classes, such as Data, DTO, VO, Bean, or Record.

nodes.label: parameter
nodes.def: Primitive: an input argument to a function or method.

nodes.label: parameter cluster
nodes.def: A subset of method parameters passed together repeatedly across different call sites.

nodes.label: passive structure
nodes.def: A class that acts merely as a data container, hosting no meaningful behavior on its data.

nodes.label: pure data container
nodes.def: The essence of a data class: state storage with no encapsulated behavior or business logic.

nodes.label: pure data structure
nodes.def: A struct-like data container with no methods, distinct from a data_class which still has accessor and mutator methods.

nodes.label: refactoring necessity
nodes.def: Conditions indicating refactoring is warranted: slow delivery, high bug rate, difficult change requests.

nodes.label: repeated fields
nodes.def: Two or more fields appearing together across multiple method signatures or class definitions.

nodes.label: temporal coupling fields
nodes.def: Fields grouped in signatures solely by call-site timing rather than semantic cohesion.

nodes.label: trivial setter
nodes.def: A setter that merely assigns a value with no validation, side effects, or consistency enforcement.
